raw_response:
I will farm this year the way I always have. My two little plots — all together not even four and a half mu — I put wheat in when the cold comes, then corn after the wheat is cut in the sixth month. Same as my husband's family did, same as everyone around here.

Seeds — my daughter-in-law takes me to the shop in town. The shop man, he sells what the others buy. For corn, everybody uses the hybrid kind now, the one in the colored bag. For wheat I take the improved kind he gives me. I don't know the names. I just take what works for the neighbors.

Fertilizer — before I plant the wheat I put one bag of the compound, the 15-15-15, on each mu. That's the bag my son carries out. Then in the spring when the wheat turns green again, I put half a bag of urea per mu. My neighbor Old Zhang does the same, maybe a little less. I put a bit more because if the wheat is hungry the harvest is bad, and then what do we eat? Wasting a little fertilizer costs some money but a bad harvest is a real disaster. For the corn, same thing — one bag of compound when I plant it, and when the corn reaches my knee my son puts another half bag of urea.

The ground — my son pays the man with the rotary machine to turn it over. Nobody uses the ox anymore, even old people like me. The machine is faster and my back cannot do it.

Water — the well is shared with the neighbors. For wheat I water three times: once before the cold, once after it greens in spring, and once when the head is coming. For corn, the summer rain usually comes, but if heaven doesn't send rain I water once or twice from the well.

Spray — my son does this, I am too old to carry the sprayer. Twice for the wheat for the little bugs and the white powder on the leaves. Twice for the corn for the borer worm.

Last year the wheat gave me maybe 450 jin per mu, the corn around 550. If heaven is kind, this year will be the same. I don't hope for more. I just don't want less.
